chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jaham, who said:
Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) brought out to me a perfume box of ebony interior in which was musk, compartmentalised from what the women would take.

key_terms.بُيُوت: Houses/rooms, here referring to compartments or sections within the box
key_terms.عَتِيدَة: Ebony or a specific type of dark, fine wood
key_terms.مَخْزَنَة: A small box or container for storing items, specifically perfume or cosmetics in this context
key_terms.مِسْك: Musk, a highly valued aromatic substance

ai.seo_question: What kind of perfume box did Imam Al-Rida (AS) possess and what was it made of?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s appreciation for refined aesthetics and practical domesticity, illustrating that luxury in Shia tradition is not merely ornamental but serves functional elegance. The specific mention of compartments for women’s use underscores the Imam’s attention to the distinct needs and customs of his community, reflecting a balanced view of material comfort within spiritual life. This narrative reinforces the concept of 'tayyibat' (good things) being permissible and encouraged for the faithful, aligning with the Imams' role as guides in both spiritual and worldly matters.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham who said,
‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> brought out to me a perfume box of ebony interior in which was musk, compartmentalised from what the women would take’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm who has said the following: “

Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once took out for me a musk container in which there was musk in an Abnus (a container made of a certain wood) container which had sections with things that women keep.’”
